note: Small talk about weather and questions about how the app works only: nothing present
turns: Hi, welcome back. What would you like to use today's time for?
Honestly not much today. I mostly logged in because the reminder popped up. Is it snowing where you are, or do you not have weather?
No weather on my side, I'm afraid. Is it snowing where you are?
First real snow of the year. The whole quad is white and the buses are running about ten minutes behind, which is normal for here.
Sounds pretty. Is there anything on your mind you would like to talk through, or would you rather keep it light today?
Keep it light. Actually I had a question. Do these sessions have a time limit, and can I see my old conversations somewhere?
There is no fixed limit on a session. Your earlier conversations are listed under the history tab on the main screen.
Okay, good to know. And does it matter if I skip a week, like over the break?
Not at all. You can pick up whenever you are back, and nothing is lost if you miss a week.
Got it. That is all I needed. I will come back next week when there is more to say.
Sounds good. Enjoy the snow, and see you next week.

note: Earlier thought-record homework completed as agreed; written cognitive work reported; avoidance mentioned only as two weeks past
turns: Good to see you again. Last time we agreed you would fill in the thought record on three evenings this week. How did that go?
I did it. Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, like we said. Thursday's was the big one, after my advisor sent back my chapter covered in comments.
What did you write down on Thursday?

The first thought was that she thinks I am not cut out for a PhD and that I am basically a fraud who slipped through admissions. Then in the evidence column I had to admit she wrote 'strong argument' twice and that she marks up everybody's drafts like that. So the balanced version was something like, the chapter needs work, which is what a draft is for.
That is a real shift from where the first thought started. How did you feel afterwards?

Less sick about it. Normally I would have spent the whole night dreading our meeting and imagining her telling me to leave the program. I still got nervous Friday morning, but it was maybe a four instead of a nine.
And how does this week compare with a couple of weeks ago?
Better, definitely. Two weeks ago I could not open her emails at all. This week I opened it the same day and answered it.
That is a meaningful change. What do you make of the 'fraud' thought now?

It still shows up. Part of me does believe I am the dumbest one in the cohort. But writing it out makes it look like a thought and not a fact, which is useful. I did not expect a worksheet to do that.
Would you want to keep going with the record this coming week?
Yes. Same three evenings, and I will add one right before the meeting on Tuesday since that is when it is worst.
Three evenings plus one before Tuesday's meeting. I will ask you about it next time.

note: Participant objects twice to breathing suggestions; assistant apologises and changes course; participant re-engages and plans (repaired). Breathing only assistant-raised
turns: Hi. How have things been since we last spoke?
Bad. The cafe cut my hours on Monday, from twenty a week down to eight, and rent is due on the first. I have about half of it.
That is a lot to land in one week. When stress spikes like this, a slow breathing exercise can help settle the body. Would you like to try one together?
Not really. I mean, breathing does not pay rent.
Fair. It can still help you think more clearly. We could do just two minutes of paced breathing and then look at the money.
You are doing it again. I told you last time too, I do not want the breathing stuff. It feels like you are not hearing what the actual problem is.
You are right, and I am sorry. You told me what the problem is and I steered away from it. Let us drop the breathing and stay on the rent. What options have you already thought about?

Okay. Thank you. So, I could ask my parents, but they are already stretched paying for my brother's braces, and my dad made a comment at Thanksgiving about how I should be standing on my own feet by now. So that one comes with a price.
So asking them costs something beyond the money. What else is on the list?

The emergency grant through the financial aid office, and picking up shifts at the library desk. I keep running the numbers in my head, like what happens if I get a late fee, then what if the landlord does not renew. It just spirals.
Which of those feels most doable first?

The grant. The office opens at nine tomorrow, so I go before my ten o'clock class and ask what paperwork they need. Then Thursday I email the library supervisor about shifts. Parents are the last resort.
That is a clear order: grant office tomorrow at nine, library email Thursday, parents only if both fall through.
Yeah. This part was actually helpful, laying it out in order. I feel like I have something to do tomorrow instead of just panicking.
I am glad. I would like to hear how the grant office goes when we next talk.

note: Lower-case transcript; long opening turns then flat one-line replies after the assistant suggests looking at the participant's part in a breakup; session ends on it (withdrawal, unresolved)
turns: Hi, I'm glad you're here. What's been going on?

um so she ended it on saturday. we were together almost three years and she did it in like a ten minute phone call, and i've just kind of been walking around in a fog since. i'm not really eating dinner, i just sit there. everything feels pointless right now, like what was the last three years even for
I'm so sorry. That is a lot to absorb in a few days. What did she say on the call?

that i was never really present, that i was always at the studio or on my phone. which, okay, some of that's true i guess, but i was working on my thesis show, it's not like i was out partying. and now i wake up at like five every morning and for a second i forget and then i remember

That sounds painful. I wonder, though, whether there is something in what she said worth taking seriously. If you were often unavailable, it might help to look honestly at your part in how this ended.
What comes up for you when you think about that?
It can be uncomfortable to look at. Would it help to list a few moments when she asked for your attention?
I may have moved too quickly there. Is there something you would rather focus on instead?
Okay. How are you feeling right now?
fine. i think i'm gonna stop for today
All right. I'm here whenever you want to come back to this.

note: Terse participant; assistant asks about sleep, mood, drinking, confiding and a walk, all denied or declined; only a roommate problem and a concrete plan are present
turns: Hello again. How has your week been?
Fine mostly. Annoyed at my roommate.
He has his girlfriend over five nights a week. She is not on the lease. Uses my dishes, leaves them. I said something once in September, nothing changed.
That sounds wearing. Is it affecting your sleep or your mood?
No. I sleep fine, I wear earplugs. I am not down about it, just irritated.
Understood. Some people in tense living situations find themselves drinking more, or staying out to avoid being home. Any of that?
I do not drink. And I am home as much as ever, it is my apartment too.
Good. Have you talked it over with anyone, a friend or someone in your family?
No. Have not brought it up with anyone. It is a dishes problem, not a crisis.
Fair enough. A short walk when the irritation builds can take the edge off. Would that be worth trying?
I would rather just fix it.
What would fixing it look like?
Talk to him Sunday night when she is gone. Say two nights a week is fine, more than that she chips in on utilities. And dishes get done same day. If he says no I go to the landlord about the lease.
That is specific and fair. Sunday night, then.
Good luck with it. Let me know how he takes it.

note: Earlier journaling task not done; assistant reframe, extension plan and retry are all deflected; avoidance, sleep loss and harsh self-judgement present
turns: Welcome back. Last session you were going to write three lines each night about what went okay that day. How did it go?
Did not happen. Forgot the first night, then it was midterms and I never started.
That is all right. What has the week been like?
Bombed the stats quiz on Wednesday. 52. Up until three most nights cramming and I am wrecked during the day, I fell asleep in lecture twice.
You are running on very little. What is still ahead of you?
A lab report that was due Friday. Have not started it. Every time I sit down I end up on my phone for two hours and then it is too late so I go to bed and feel like garbage about it.
What goes through your mind when you sit down to it?
That I am lazy. Everybody else in the section turned theirs in. I am just the useless one who cannot do basic things.
That is a harsh verdict. Another way to see it: anyone sleeping four hours a night would struggle to start a report. Does that fit at all?
Maybe. Does not change that it is late.
True. Would it help to email the TA today and ask for a short extension?
I guess I could. I do not know.
Okay. Would you be willing to give the three lines another try this week, even on one night?
No promises needed. We can look at where things stand next time.

note: Two pieces of earlier work: grounding done twice instead of daily, call to counselling centre not made (partial). Grief, faith, pastor as support, a named barrier, then a scheduled commitment to call
turns: Hello. When we last talked you planned two things: the grounding exercise each morning, and calling the counselling centre to ask about their grief group. How did those go?
Half and half. I did the grounding twice, Tuesday and Thursday, not every day. And I did not call. I had the number up on my phone three different times and put it down.
Two mornings is still two mornings. What happened on those days?

It helped a little, to be honest. Thursday I was in the parking structure before class and could not make myself get out of the car, and naming things I could see got me moving. The other days I just forgot or did not care enough.
And the call. What got in the way?

I keep thinking a grief group is for people who lost a child or a spouse. My dad was sixty-eight and sick for a year. It has been two months. I feel like I would be taking a seat from someone with a real reason.
There is no ranking that decides whose loss is real enough. How have these two months been for you?

I cry in the shower most mornings so my kids do not see. Some days there is just nothing in me, I go through class and dinner like a machine. And I worry about my mom rattling around that house alone, she will not let any of us stay over.
You are carrying your own grief and watching hers. Is there anyone you have been able to lean on?

I talked to my pastor after the service on Sunday. I told him I am angry, that I prayed for a year for my dad to get better and it feels like nobody was listening. He did not try to fix it, he just said the anger was allowed. That was more than I expected.
It sounds like being heard mattered. Coming back to the group, where does that leave you?
I know. I will call. Monday at ten, I have a gap between classes, I will do it from the car before I can talk myself out of it.
Monday at ten, from the car. And the grounding?
I will keep doing it on class mornings, that is when I need it.
Then that is the plan. I will ask about both next time.

note: Grounding exercise carried out live and committed to for tomorrow; medication and psychiatrist as current care; sleep asked about and denied as a problem; bodily anxiety is not physical health
turns: Hi there. What brings you in today?
My thesis defense is tomorrow at two and I cannot settle. My heart has been pounding since I woke up and I keep picturing myself blanking on the first question in front of the committee.
That sounds intense. How have you been sleeping in the run-up?
Sleep is okay actually. Seven hours last night. It is the daytime that is the problem.
Good to know. Is there other support in place for you right now?

I started sertraline about three weeks ago. My psychiatrist said it could take a month or so to notice anything, and I see her again next Wednesday. So that is in motion, it just does not help me tomorrow.
Would you like to try a short grounding exercise now, something you could reuse tomorrow?
Sure, I will try anything at this point.
Start by naming five things you can see.
My laptop, a coffee ring on the desk, the printed slides, a blue highlighter, and the neighbour's bike through the window.
Now four things you can feel.
The chair under my legs, my sleeves, my feet on the floor, the edge of the desk under my wrists.
And three things you can hear.
The radiator ticking, somebody's music down the hall, and my own breathing I guess.
How is your body now compared with a few minutes ago?
Slower. My heart is not hammering like it was. Okay, that did more than I thought it would.
Could you see yourself using it tomorrow?
Yes. I will do it in the hallway right before they call me in, the full five senses.
Good. I hope the defense goes well.

note: Lower-case transcript; loneliness, cohort left-out, nightly drinking and broken sleep; counselling and exercise raised by the assistant and not taken up; running described as stopped
turns: Hi. What's on your mind this evening?

uh i don't really know where to start. i moved here in august for the program and it's been like three months and i basically don't talk to anybody outside of lab. like i go whole weekends without saying a word out loud. it's really isolating
That sounds like a lonely stretch. What are the people in your program like?

they're fine, they're nice. but everybody in my cohort kind of already paired off into their groups the first couple weeks, and i missed that window i think. they go to trivia on thursdays and i hear about it on friday, you know
Hearing about it afterwards stings. How do your evenings usually go?

so that's the other thing. i've been having like three or four beers most nights. it started as one to wind down and now it's kind of just what the evening is. and then i wake up at four and can't get back to sleep, and i skip the morning seminar cause i feel rough
Thank you for telling me. Do you feel concerned about the drinking?
a little yeah. it's more than i ever drank in undergrad
Is there someone you could tell about how this has been, a labmate or someone in your family?
no. i can't tell the people in lab, they'd just think i'm a mess, and i have to work with them for five years
That makes sense as a worry. The campus counselling service sees a lot of graduate students for exactly this. Would you consider it?
Some people find exercise helps fill the evenings. Have you tried anything like that?
i used to run back home. haven't since i moved
Would you want to pick one evening this week to do something different?
i'll think about it. maybe thursday, when they're all at trivia anyway
Thursday could be a good one. No pressure either way, and I'm glad you said all this out loud.

note: Mild complaint about a platitude; assistant concedes; participant re-engages at length (repaired). Injury, team as social life, low mood, drawing as coping; running stopped, teammates not told
turns: Hi, good to have you back. How are things?
Mixed. The MRI came back last week and it is a torn meniscus, so surgery in January and no soccer until at least the summer. I am on crutches around campus, which in the snow is a joke.
I am sorry, that is rough news. What has it been like being off the pitch?

Harder than the knee itself, honestly. The club team is basically my whole social life here. They still have practice Tuesdays and Thursdays and the group chat is all inside jokes from games I was not at. Nobody is being mean, I am just suddenly on the outside of it.
That is a real loss of routine and connection. It is important to stay positive and remember that injuries are temporary. Many people find new strengths during recovery.
That is kind of a poster-on-the-wall answer, no offense. I know it is temporary. That does not make the next six months less flat.
You are right, that was glib. I skipped past what you actually said. Tell me about flat.

Thanks. Flat is like, I get back from class and there is nothing to look forward to. Running was how I burned off a bad day and that is gone too. I have been pretty down, most evenings I just sit with the knee up and nothing sounds good.
So you lost the team and the thing you used to manage bad days, both at once. Has anything helped, even a little?

One thing. I dug out my old sketchbook over the weekend and drew for a couple of hours, and it was the first time in two weeks I was not thinking about the knee. I might keep that up on practice nights so I am not just sitting there checking the chat.
Putting something of your own into practice nights makes sense. Have you let any teammates know how this has been for you?
Not yet. I have not said anything to them.
That is okay. It is there if you want it later.
Yeah. Okay. This was better than I expected after that first bit.
I appreciate you telling me when I missed. Take care of the knee.

note: Improvement and coping the participant started on their own: nothing was set in an earlier session, so follow-up is not_discussed; a dreaded conversation that went fine is progress, not anxiety
turns: Hi. How has the past week been for you?
Good, actually. Noticeably better than when we talked last. I think the heaviness lifted a bit, I still have grey mornings but they pass by lunch now instead of taking the whole day.
I am glad to hear that. What do you think made the difference?

A couple of things I just started doing on my own. I have been walking the river trail after my shift, forty minutes or so, and I come back with a clearer head every time. And I am sleeping through the night again, which I had not done since about September.
Those are big changes. Anything else?

I finally told my friend from the dorm how rough the autumn had been. I had been hiding it from her for months. She came over with soup and we talked until midnight, and she said she had wondered why I kept cancelling.
How was it to say it out loud to her?
Scary for about thirty seconds and then a relief. I was dreading that conversation more than almost anything, and it went fine.
That took something. It sounds like she was glad to be let in.
Also I started baking again on Sundays. Bread mostly. It is the one thing where I stop checking the clock, so I am keeping that in the week on purpose.
Would you like to set anything for the coming week?
Just keep the walks going, four days, and bake Sunday. I do not want to add anything new and jinx it.
Four walks and Sunday bread. That sounds like enough.
Thanks. It is nice to have somewhere to say this out loud.
I am glad you did. See you next week.

note: Assistant raises sleep, appetite, family and counselling: denied, brushed past or turned down with a reason (help_barrier). Participant works a thought record live in the chat; faith and romantic decision are the topics
turns: Hello. What would you like to focus on today?

My boyfriend proposed two weeks ago and I said I needed time. I have not been able to give him an answer and it is eating at me. I keep going back and forth, and I am terrified of choosing wrong and finding out in ten years.
That is a heavy decision to hold. How are your sleep and appetite?
Both normal. I am functioning fine, I just cannot decide.
And your family, how do they feel about him?
They like him. That is not really the issue.

I have fasted and prayed about it three times now and I do not feel anything either way. In my church you are supposed to get a confirmation about something this big, and everyone talks like theirs came clear as day. So either I am doing it wrong or the silence is the answer, and I cannot tell which.
That silence sounds hard to sit in. Some people find it useful to talk a decision like this through with a counsellor. Is that something you would consider?
No, I do not think so. It is not a mental health thing, and a counsellor on campus is not going to understand the faith side of it anyway.
Understood. Would you be open to working through one thought with me, step by step? Pick the thought that hits hardest.
Okay. The thought is: if he were the right one I would feel sure by now.
What is the evidence for that thought?
My sister says she knew within a month. And I felt sure about choosing my major and about moving here right away.

I was not sure about my major, now that I think about it, I switched twice. And I am slow with every big decision, I took four months to pick an apartment. Also when I picture him not being around, that feels clearly wrong.
So what would a more balanced version of the thought be?

Maybe that being unsure is how I do every decision, so it does not say much about him. Not feeling a lightning bolt is not the same as a no. That is a useful way to put it, I had not separated those two things before.
That is a clear distinction, and it is yours. Take it with you this week.
